architectureDecisions: The canonical accessible-next resolver is the only terminal enablement authority; no accessible /artbreeze preserves the exact existing wrapped 48-second CoScroll behavior.
The single CoScroll input owner drives timeline -> terminal-hold -> terminal-exit -> committing; the event that first reaches progress 1 cannot also advance exit.
Motion epochs, physical event ids, reverse cancellation, access loss, and a post-transition quiet window reject stale GSAP, timer, input-inertia, and readiness work.
Rotation signals are generation-aware pending/live/fallback snapshots; matching finite angle/speed must arrive within 500ms or the terminal attempt latches fallback.
The source GLB remains opaque and retains real negative Y-yaw while surface-sampled pale-jade particles replace its cut-out strokes; the glyph is never flattened into a rotating screen plane.
Live and fallback paths map into the existing strict chapter-visual-handoff-v1 coscroll-ring union without changing its shape.
A transition-layer DOM ring is only a transport owner between source-ring completion and verified film ownership; it does not persist into the selected B edit.
Destination reset receives an explicit coordinator/history/direct/source-recovery reason so CoScroll back restores terminal-hold while direct access and refresh restore 10.2/48.
Successful takeover requires the real verified ArtBreeze first-sequence MP4 to decode its n=355 first frame; poster-only readiness is fallback evidence, not CP2.3 success.
The frozen B-v9 media, letterbox, four-frame exposure, text, sound carrier, and DOM/video ownership remain authoritative through CP2.1, CP2.2, CP2.3, and CP2.4.
